name: MLOps
description: Taking models to production: reproducibility, experiment tracking, serving, ML pipelines with CI/CD and monitoring.

nodes.name: ML lifecycle
nodes.desc: The path from experiment to production model and where ML systems fail.
nodes.summary: You will understand the stages a model goes through from experiment to production and the common ways ML systems fail.
topics: Hidden technical debt in ML systems

nodes.name: MLOps principles
nodes.desc: Automation, versioning, testing and monitoring as practices, and maturity levels.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain the core MLOps practices of automation, versioning, testing and monitoring and assess a team's maturity level.
topics: Roles across data science and engineering

nodes.name: Reproducible envs
nodes.desc: Pinned dependencies, lock files, random seeds and deterministic training.
nodes.summary: You will be able to make training runs reproducible with pinned dependencies, lock files, fixed seeds and deterministic settings.

nodes.name: Data versioning
nodes.desc: Versioning datasets and features alongside code.
nodes.summary: You will be able to version datasets and features alongside code so any model can be traced back to its exact data.

nodes.name: Experiment tracking
nodes.desc: Logging parameters, metrics and artefacts to compare runs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to log parameters, metrics and artefacts for each training run and compare runs to choose the best model.

nodes.name: Feature stores
nodes.desc: Sharing consistent features between training and serving.
nodes.summary: You will understand how feature stores keep feature definitions consistent between training and serving.

nodes.name: Model registry
nodes.desc: Versioned models, stages, approvals and lineage.
nodes.summary: You will be able to manage model versions in a registry with stages, approvals and lineage back to their training runs.

nodes.name: Packaging models
nodes.desc: Serialising models and packaging them with their runtime into containers.
nodes.summary: You will be able to serialise trained models and package them with their runtime dependencies into containers.
topics: Packaging inference code with the model

nodes.name: Model serving
nodes.desc: Online and batch inference, REST and gRPC endpoints, and latency budgets.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose between online and batch inference and expose models through REST or gRPC endpoints within latency budgets.

nodes.name: Faster inference
nodes.desc: Quantisation, compilation, batching and hardware choices.
nodes.summary: You will be able to speed up model inference with quantisation, compilation, batching and appropriate hardware choices.

nodes.name: Serve a model
nodes.desc: Containerise a trained model and serve it behind a documented API with load tests.
nodes.summary: You will containerise a trained model, serve it behind a documented API and load-test it to measure latency and throughput.
topics: Load testing for latency and throughput

nodes.name: Training pipelines
nodes.desc: Orchestrated, repeatable pipelines from data to registered model.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build orchestrated training pipelines that repeatably turn raw data into a registered model.

nodes.name: CI/CD for ML
nodes.desc: Automated tests, training and gated promotion of models.
nodes.summary: You will be able to set up CI/CD for ML that tests code, retrains models and promotes them only when they pass quality gates.

nodes.name: Testing ML systems
nodes.desc: Data tests, model behaviour tests and infrastructure tests.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test ML systems at the data, model and infrastructure levels to catch problems before production.

nodes.name: ML on Kubernetes
nodes.desc: Scaling training jobs and inference services on a cluster.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run training jobs and scalable inference services on Kubernetes with GPUs and autoscaling.

nodes.name: Model monitoring
nodes.desc: Tracking latency, errors, prediction distributions and business metrics.
nodes.summary: You will be able to monitor deployed models by tracking latency, errors, prediction distributions and business metrics with alerts.
topics: Delayed ground truth and accuracy tracking

nodes.name: Drift detection
nodes.desc: Detecting data and concept drift with statistical tests.
nodes.summary: You will be able to detect data drift and concept drift in production using statistical tests and distribution distances.

nodes.name: Retraining loops
nodes.desc: Triggered and scheduled retraining, shadow deployments and rollbacks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to keep models current with scheduled or triggered retraining and release them safely with shadow deployments and rollbacks.

nodes.name: Responsible ML
nodes.desc: Fairness audits, explainability, model cards and governance.
nodes.summary: You will be able to audit models for fairness, explain their predictions and document them with model cards under clear governance.

nodes.name: End-to-end MLOps
nodes.desc: Build a pipeline that trains, deploys, monitors and retrains a model automatically.
nodes.summary: You will build an automated system that trains, deploys, monitors and retrains a model end to end.
